claim: For binary three-dimensional functional batch codes in which every request in every five-request multiset has a pairwise-disjoint recovery set of size at most two, the minimum length is exactly \(11\). Equivalently, a \([11,3,5,2]\) code exists and no \([n,3,5,2]\) code exists for \(n\le 10\).

correctness.rationale: The repeated-query formula is exact because every binary minimal recovery set of size at most two is a singleton q or a complementary pair u,v with u+v=q. Summing over the seven q gives n plus the pair-minimum sum. Balancing bounds that sum by 24 at total n=10, yielding 34<35. The explicit rank-three length-eleven witness is exhaustively verified on all 462 query multisets; the checker also independently enumerates all 8008 total-ten multiplicity vectors.

evidence: arXiv:2508.02586 studies minimum functional-batch length with unrestricted recovery size; the Tartu thesis reports unrestricted k=3,t=5 minimum 10.
arXiv:2601.12302 studies bounded recovery-set size and derives general lower bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted exact value does not dominate the locality-two problem because its recovery sets may be larger than two. The bounded-recovery general theory does not state a stronger theorem implying exact length 11 at this parameter.

value.rationale: The parameter is structurally motivated: k=3 has the length-seven simplex locality-two code at four requests and a length-fourteen doubled-simplex construction at eight requests. Five requests are the first intermediate count, and the exact value 11 measures a genuine one-column penalty relative to the known unrestricted value 10. The repeated-query capacity argument is reusable and not a table recomputation.
